Quick Summary

Desert Solitaire is a 1968 book by American writer Edward Abbey . The work is considered his best by many and is set in the southwestern United States, primarily reflecting an uncompromising environmentalist philosophy. 1
Abbey's experiences as a park ranger and fire lookout for the National Park Service in the southwest provided him with an intimate understanding of the region's landscape. This perspective shaped his writing, allowing him to observe both ancient cultures and the encroachment of modern civilization. Desert Solitaire is an extended meditation on the wilderness of southeastern Utah and the human impact on it. The book, along with his novel The Monkey Wrench Gang , became influential in the environmental movement. 1 2
